hints: Look at the starting molecule carefully, it has two different functional groups that can both be oxidised.
Recall what excess acidified dichromate under reflux does to a primary alcohol and separately to an aldehyde.
Apply full oxidation to both ends of the 2-carbon chain and think about what HOOC-COOH looks like in skeletal form.
walkthrough:
**Spot the two oxidisable groups**

Great start, let us read the structure. $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CHO}$ has a primary alcohol on the left ($-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) and an aldehyde on the right ($-\text{CHO}$).

Starting molecule:
$$\text{HO-CH}_2\text{-CHO}$$

**Recall the strong oxidation rules**

With excess acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ heated under reflux, oxidation goes all the way to the end with no stopping halfway.

Rules to remember:
$$\text{primary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{aldehyde} \rightarrow \text{carboxylic acid}$$
$$\text{aldehyde} \rightarrow \text{carboxylic acid}$$

**Oxidise both ends fully**

Now apply that to both ends. The $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ becomes $-\text{COOH}$ and the $-\text{CHO}$ also becomes $-\text{COOH}$.

Overall change:
$$\text{HOCH}_2\text{CHO} \rightarrow \text{HOOC-COOH}$$
This is ethanedioic acid, with two carboxylic acid groups joined directly together.

options.A: Incorrect. This is $\text{HOOC-CH}_2\text{-COOH}$ (propanedioic acid) which has three carbons. The starting material only has two carbons, so we cannot gain a carbon during oxidation.
options.B: Correct. Both groups are fully oxidised to carboxylic acids to give $\text{HOOC-COOH}$ (ethanedioic acid). The skeletal drawing shows two $\text{C=O}$ groups joined together, each with an $\text{OH}$, which matches complete oxidation.
options.C: Incorrect. This is $\text{HOCH}_2\text{COOH}$ where only the aldehyde has been oxidised and the primary alcohol is unchanged. With excess reagent under reflux, the primary alcohol would also be oxidised to a carboxylic acid.
options.D: Incorrect. This is $\text{OHC-COOH}$ (actually drawn as $\text{O=CH-COOH}$) where one end is still an aldehyde. This is only partial oxidation. Under reflux with excess oxidant, no aldehyde would remain.
